Project delivery

After you’ve been awarded funding and signed the works package deed, we’ll ask you to enter into a works contract with the main contractor.

Arrangements where third parties who are not the applicant, enter into a works contract on the applicant’s behalf will only be accepted in exceptional circumstances (for example, where two entities are responsible for works on different parts of the building). In such cases, we may ask for additional documentation showing how the funding we’ve provided is distributed between multiple entities, and their associated responsibilities.

One party cannot provide full consultancy services and act as, or appoint, the lead contractor. We’ve laid out below works contract requirements and other information you’ll need throughout your project.

Works contract requirements

The works contract should include the following:

A principal designer, for the purposes of Construction Design and Management Regulations 2015 (CDM Regs), must be named in the works contract and must meet the level of competence outlined in the regulations.

A contract administrator (CA), employer’s agent (EA) or architect must be named in the works contract. They must be responsible for administering the contract for the duration for the works. The CA, EA or architect must be a member of a chartered professional body (i.e. RICS, RIBA, CIOB etc) and appropriately experienced for the scale of the proposed works.

The main contractor named in the works contract must be appointed as the principal contractor under the Construction Design and Management Regulations 2015 (CDM Regs). The principal contractor must meet the level of competence described in the regulations and, if requested, evidence must be produced to verify this.

A quantity surveyor or cost consultant must be named in the contract and be responsible for contract valuations and cost monitoring. The quantity surveyor or cost consultant must be a member of a relevant chartered professional body (i.e. RICS).

A defects rectification period of a minimum of 12 months must be included in the contract and a minimum of 2.5% of the overall works contract value must be held as retention for this period. In addition, the works contract must include a provision for a minimum of 5% of the overall works contract value to be held as retention from commencement until practical completion of the works.

Adequate professional indemnity insurance must be stipulated in the works contract if the contractor is responsible for any design work. Its protection must cover the nature of the works and must not exclude cladding.

The contract must include an arbitration and/or adjudication procedure for dispute resolution.

The works contract must be executed as a deed, and this forms the works package deed. Evidence will need to be available on request that the contract has been executed as a deed to provide the maximum latent defects liability period.

Planning and building control

As part of any application, you should contact local authorities[footnote 9] and building control to facilitate the timely completion of design and development work to achieve an early start on site.

There will be a lead-in time to apply for and obtain planning permission. Your professional team will be able to advise you if planning permission is needed for your proposed works. Planning permission is distinct from building regulations approval which will always be required.

Building regulations

Building work carried out on a building must meet building regulations (The Building Regulations 2010), including minimum standards for fire safety and energy efficiency. (Please note these may be amended from time to time and following the introduction of secondary legislation pursuant to Part 3 of the Building Safety Act 2022.)

To ensure energy efficiency standards, building works to the external envelope of a building should adequately account for any changes in thermal bridges which may occur because of the work. They must also maintain or enhance the thermal performance of the external envelope of a building, where technically and economically feasible.

You may also wish to consider if there is an opportunity to use the project as a low-cost way to implement further energy efficiency measures that go beyond the current minimum requirements of the building regulations. Implementing other low-cost energy efficiency measures at the same time as works relating to the life safety fire risks associated with cladding may save you further cost and resource in the future. This is not mandatory and will not be considered as a condition of receiving funding. Any additional costs for these works, above those recommended in the FRAEW, should not form part of your application for CSS funding.

Schedule of works

Initial pre-tender support may have been paid to you upfront. The remaining grant award to enable you to complete the works will be paid monthly in arrears based on submission of your claims containing evidence of expenditure. Your chosen contractor must be made aware of the monthly payments schedule (in arrears) during the procurement process. They must also agree with the reporting schedule to enable applicants to meet the terms of the grant funding agreement.

Following the approval of the works package, the signing of the works package deed with Homes England and entering into the works contract, you will then need to create your schedule of works.

At this stage we will be asking for further information about your project delivery, which includes:

providing the signed works contract

Let us know that you intend to decant residents as soon as possible and definitely ahead of the Works Package stage.

Decanting residents for remediation works should be a last resort when no other option is available and not a choice. The decant must be planned thoroughly to mitigate the impact to residents. This can be done by:

partially phasing remediation works

decanting only essential units

This helps to lessen the time residents must live elsewhere and ensures value for money is achieved.

You will be asked to provide a sufficiently detailed decant strategy.

You should consider and evidence:

why any form of decant is needed — noting that CSS only funds this if it is essential to undertaking the eligible works

the options you have considered for the phasing and level of decant, and why you have arrived at this decision

You should detail the options you have considered for alternative accommodation, with serviced accommodation only proposed when all other options are not viable. For example:

use of vacant units in the block for partial or phased decants

engagement with residents and leaseholders to determine alternative arrangements such as staying with family and friends at a reduced cost

ensuring that alternative temporary accommodation reflects the basics of the existing accommodation (the same number of bedrooms, for example)

You must also consider and evidence the number of owner-occupied versus privately rented units.

For privately rented units, assess how many individual landlords this relates to and whether the Responsible Entity or any linked parties own any of these units.

CSS will not fund any loss of rental income arising from remediation works for landlords. It is the responsibility of all parties to manage tenancies effectively to mitigate their own loss.

We expect to see strong leaseholder and resident engagement delivered throughout.

Compiling your works package

Once the grant funding agreement is signed and you have started the monthly progress reports, you will be able to start compiling your works package.

Submit your works package at the same time as you make your submission to Building Control (if your works require it).

The first time you open the works package in the Building Remediation Hub it will be populated with information from the matching section in your most recent progress report. You should only open the section when you are ready to complete it. Updates in future progress reports will not update the works package in turn.

Including information already provided in your progress report, to complete the works package you will need to provide:

full details of your appointed project team including their contact information

confirmation of your grant certifying officer (read ‘The grant certifying officer and duty of care deed’)

planning permission progress

a Fire Risk Assessment and details of an internal defects if not already submitted at initial application stage

proposed works to cladding

a full proposed cost schedule (read ‘Cost schedule’)

details of any third-party financial contributions to the project

significant dates for project including start on site, date of cladding removal, as appropriate and completion date

You will need to appoint a professional team, scope the project and develop a works specification. The pre-tender support payment is designed to help with this and you should have the correct project team in place to begin this stage.

When you appoint your team, your lead designer will have the main responsibility for designing and specifying the works. Who fulfils this role can vary depending on the type of construction contract proposed. If your professional team is carrying out all the design and specification of the works, it’s likely that the lead designer will be a member of the team such as an architect or a façade engineer. If you are advised to use a ‘Design and Build’ type contract, the lead contractor may also carry out much of the design and will be the lead designer.

You must not appoint any party who was involved with the original works which are now being addressed by the CSS without prior specific agreement from Homes England. Consent will only be given by exception where we’re satisfied that appointing someone associated with the original installation is appropriate.

The grant certifying officer and duty of care deed

You will need to nominate either your quantity surveyor or project manager to act as the grant certifying officer[footnote 7] for your project. The grant certifying officer and their ‘consultant’ firm must be independent of the Responsible Entity and the contractor. The grant certifying officer will sign off individual grant claims and must:

be qualified in their field

be a member of a professional body

hold professional indemnity insurance

be knowledgeable and have significant experience relevant to the specific technical aspects

The firm that your grant certifying officer works for will need to enter into a duty of care deed with the Responsible Entity and Homes England. The duty of care deed is a legal document. It ensures that the individual and the firm[footnote 8] who sign off monthly grant claims have a duty of care to Homes England in undertaking the work as well as their responsibility to their client.

A template duty of care deed is made available so that the grant certifying officer firm can see the terms. This is for information only. We will send the actual document to be signed when appropriate.

If the grant certifying officer and, or, the firm they work for changes during the course of your project, let us know as soon as possible by emailing support@claddingsafetyscheme.co.uk. Quote the application reference number and building name in your email.

If cost variations are being sought, you must retain information to prove that the cost variations relate only to the works permitted for grant funding and/or works needed to facilitate them.

We’ll rely on your grant certifying officer to rigorously check all costs and they’ll have to enter into a duty of care agreement with Homes England.

Practical completion — scheme exit

At the point of practical completion for your project, and ahead of your final payment being made, you must submit a closing report using the Building Remediation Hub.

Your report must provide Homes England with evidence covering all of the following points.

Total project spend

This must be signed off by your grant certifying officer with all supporting evidence provided.

Homes England may use independent cost consultants to fully review project spend to provide assurance it is in line with the grant award and covers eligible works only. The cumulative funding figure will be published on the subsidy transparency database.

Building control sign off

This must be signed off by the appropriate regulatory body.

Homes England will not make final payments until the relevant certification has been provided.

It is the responsibility of the applicant to work with their contractors to ensure that any part of the works requiring action is satisfactorily addressed and fully signed off.

Practical completion certification

Evidence of practical completion certification must be provided.

An updated Fire Risk Assessment (FRA)

The Fire Risk Assessment must be updated and show eligible works identified in the Fire Risk Appraisal of External Wall (FRAEW) have been completed, including who carried these out and when.

The evacuation strategy must be updated after any works identified in the FRAEW have been carried out.

Sign off from Building Control is needed and must show works have reduced the risk-to-life rating to a tolerable level.

Blocks of flats also require a Fire Risk Assessment to be in place. Homes England uses the established process and documentation required for management of each building. The Responsible Entity must determine the type of FRA that is appropriate as part of their ongoing management of the building.

Informing residents and leaseholders about the completion of the remediation project

You must include evidence of communicating to residents and leaseholders about completion of the remediation project.

You must include a link to the Cladding Safety Scheme — Leaseholder and residents’ survey (Hosted on Microsoft Forms) as part of this communication.

Your position in relation to clause 5.4 of the Grant Funding Arrangement

As part of your report you must set out your position in relation to clause 5.4 of the Grant Funding Arrangement in as much detail as you can.

You must include all entities including:

the developer

any supply chain party

any warranty provider

Public funds have been provided to enable early remediation and ensuring these can be recovered is part of your contractual obligation. Including the most recent supporting evidence or correspondence will allow us to do this.

Building insurance

You’ll be asked to provide buildings insurance documentation upon completion of your remediation works. This will include:

the total sum insured

the insurance premium

the name of the insurance provider

Sharing this information helps Homes England and Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government report on post-remediation benefits and changes to premiums.

Open book access

The CSS processes follow the government’s approach to open-book contract management. These help Homes England maintain a clear line of sight between the cost requirements for eligible works compared to the Homes England funds granted. A low cost, minimal open-book approach is applied, which gives us assurance that value for money is being achieved, as required by Managing Public Money for Government grant schemes.

Therefore, you’ll need to submit any relevant supporting documents requested by Homes England. You’ll need to keep on record any other documents that you’ve confirmed you have obtained so they are available on request. The grant funding agreement stipulates that Homes England and appointed third parties are given access to required information and documentation.

During works, Homes England has the right to request from you cost details and any supporting documentation. The CSS will retain specialist support (e.g., legal, commercial, technical advisors) who will have the same open book access rights.

After completion, a sample of projects may be randomly selected or targeted for potential government audit activities (e.g. National Audit Office value-for-money studies). You’ll be responsible for providing your own resources for these audits. We recommend that you allow for this potential scope in your consultants’ appointments. Funding such activity is not an eligible cost.

Complaints

If you have a complaint about the application process, please see the Homes England complaints procedure.
